correctness.rationale: Each private leaf has only its support vertex as a neighbor, so domination forces at least one selected vertex from every disjoint support-leaf pair and therefore at least n selected vertices. Semipaired sets are even, giving the least-even-at-least-n lower bound. For every spanning tree, a longest-path reduction pairs either two sibling leaves at distance two or a unique leaf with its support at distance one, deletes the pair, and preserves a tree; induction yields floor(n/2) disjoint distance-at-most-two pairs. These pairs remain distance at most two in the base graph. All original vertices therefore attain the lower bound for even n, while adding the private leaf of the sole unmatched original vertex attains it for odd n. Exhaustive optimum checks on all connected labeled base graphs through order five confirm the formula.

value.rationale: The result covers the leaf corona of every connected graph with one uniform exact formula, rather than a narrow named family. The private-leaf lower bound alone does not solve semipaired domination because parity and pairability remain; the tree-square matching lemma supplies exactly the missing global structure. The theorem therefore converts a nontrivial domination-and-pairing optimization problem into a closed form on a standard graph operation and provides an explicit construction.
